currentContext.business: RAIN converts byproducts of oil refining (green petroleum coke) and steel production (coal tar) into high-value carbon-based products (CPC, CTP and other carbon products) used as critical raw materials by the aluminium, graphite, carbon black, wood preservation, titanium dioxide and refractory industries. Its Advanced Materials segment further transforms a portion of this carbon output plus petrochemicals into engineered products, chemical intermediates and resins for specialty chemicals, coatings, construction, automotive and petroleum customers, while its Cement segment manufactures and markets OPC and PPC for civil construction and infrastructure within India.

currentContext.strengths: Vertically-integrated, global-scale organisation providing a platform to develop higher-margin downstream products|Scale and process sophistication give flexibility to source raw materials from a wide range of geographies and adjust product mix to meet stringent customer specifications|Global manufacturing footprint and integrated worldwide logistics network positioned to address raw material supply and product demand on a global basis in both established and emerging markets|Established supplier to the Chinese battery market with years of experience serving major manufacturers, positioning RAIN in the emerging Battery Anode Material (BAM) space|Global shared-service centre in India supporting SAP ERP usage across all global facilities, enabling effective internal controls and timely reporting
currentContext.strategies: Diversification across Carbon, Advanced Materials and Cement segments to balance risk and mitigate challenges within individual businesses|Continued emphasis on investment discipline and structural optimisation, including deferring the proposed brownfield expansion of the Cement segment to reassess short-, medium- and long-term regional demand fundamentals before initiating it at a more appropriate time|In Advanced Materials, gradual increase in participation in higher-value downstream applications (including an initial foray into energy-storage-linked materials) while leveraging core carbon processing expertise|Operational discipline via resource efficiency initiatives, optimum raw material utilisation and prudent capital expenditure management|Energy efficiency initiatives including expansions in solar power capacity and energy recovery systems as part of a gradual decarbonisation and long-term energy security approach|Continued thrust on financial stability and cash discipline: capex directed primarily toward maintenance requirements and efficiency improvements, avoiding major acquisitions and unrelated expansion, and focusing on strengthening the balance sheet and improving cash generation|Strengthened governance oversight: Board directed management to undertake a comprehensive review of operating segments and key processes, and led structured governance reviews covering risk mitigation, regulatory compliance and operational resilience|Process improvement and development of new, higher-margin products and technologies through R&D; combining purchasing, trading, plant operations, logistics management, finance and R&D functions within each segment; executing cost-reduction initiatives|Leveraging the scale of the vertically-integrated organisation as a platform to continue developing higher-margin downstream products and realise economies of scale|Growth capital deployed selectively in line with clear return thresholds and regional demand visibility, while maintenance capex and safety investments remain non-negotiable across facilities|Brownfield cement plant expansion in Telangana approached with prudence: execution phased in line with market absorption, no expenditure incurred to date, and continued evaluation of opportunities to optimise project costs while preserving the strategic advantage of the expansion|The Board ratified an interim dividend of ₹1 per equity share for the financial year ended December 31, 2025. As part of its governance oversight, the Board periodically reviews strategy and business plans, annual operating and capital expenditure budgets, and investment and exposure limits, alongside performance of operating divisions and significant transactions, as the framework through which capital deployment decisions are overseen.
currentContext.expansion: During 2025, RAIN received the necessary permissions to initiate a brownfield expansion at its Cement segment's site in Suryapet, India, which will increase clinker capacity from 1.0 to 2.5 million tonnes and expand waste-heat recovery electricity capacity from 5 MW to 12 MW; total cement capacity remained at 4.0 million tonnes across operations in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh pending this expansion. Alongside the Suryapet project, RAIN progressed captive renewable/solar power initiatives at its cement plants (including an onsite solar power capacity expansion of 2.10 MW near a plant) and continued logistics optimisation. For 2026, strategic focus areas at the Cement segment include cost competitiveness through freight optimisation, strengthened quality assurance, upgraded laboratories and additional solar electricity generation, 'supporting the future and a new production line'. RAIN also initiated development of a net-zero roadmap for the Cement segment in collaboration with the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), currently in a baseline-establishment phase covering emissions, water and waste. On the Advanced Materials/Carbon side, RAIN established the Rain Technology Innovation Center in Hamilton, Ontario for carbon-based anode material development and testing, and is running multiple publicly funded R&D projects (OVIN, NGen, CMIF, Canada-Germany ZIM) on graphite purification, coating, upcycling and sustainable supply chains, alongside a North American demonstration facility supporting entry into Battery Anode Material (BAM) markets. Named capex-linked upgrades at the Lake Charles facility include boiler economiser modification/upgrade, boiler feedwater heat exchanger upgrade, baghouse MCC HVAC upgrade and wastewater pretreatment improvements.

risks.risk: Heavy revenue concentration in the Carbon segment
risks.note: About 74% of RAIN Group's consolidated revenue for CY 2025 was generated from the Carbon business segment, making overall performance highly dependent on CPC/CTP pricing and volume cycles.

risks.risk: Foreign-exchange exposure across a global, multi-currency footprint
risks.note: Realisations and EBITDA were materially affected by currency movements in CY 2025 - the Euro appreciated 9% and the US Dollar 4% against the Indian Rupee, which flattered results this year but implies a reverse drag if these currencies depreciate against the Rupee.

risks.risk: Cyclical demand weakness in the Advanced Materials segment
risks.note: Advanced Materials volumes fell approximately 7% in CY 2025 on lower throughput of engineered products and chemical intermediates due to weaker demand, showing the segment's sensitivity to downstream customer demand cycles.

risks.risk: Regional demand softness and falling capacity utilisation in Cement
risks.note: The Cement segment's average capacity utilisation declined from approximately 71% in PY2024 to approximately 64% in CY2025, with market conditions across South India remaining mixed amid muted infrastructure-led construction activity.

risks.risk: Concentration of global IT/shared-services infrastructure in a single location
risks.note: RAIN has established a single global shared-service center in India to support SAP users across all its global facilities, concentrating a critical operational and financial-reporting function in one jurisdiction.

one-line thesis: CPC margins improved sharply due to China's supply crunch and India's lifted 6-year import ban, boosting Carbon segment EBITDA by 1.63B INR; however, Advanced Materials and Cement segments underperformed due to raw material shortages and market consolidation, delaying full margin recovery.

themes.title: Refractories & metallurgical consumables
themes.need: Refractory and metallurgical-consumable makers earn recurring per-tonne pricing tied to steel/cement OUTPUT volumes - an annuity-like wear-parts thesis, not the producers own realisation cycle. Q1FY27 turned the graphite-electrode leg on PRICE rather than demand: HEG's standalone EBITDA swung from -INR 126cr in Q4FY26 to +INR 211cr at a 29% margin on LOWER volumes, entirely realisation and mix, after GrafTech announced $600-1,200/t and Tokai $930/t electrode price increases. The timing is unusually favourable - HEG's own price rises only take effect from October because its book is committed through Sept/Oct, while needle-coke inflation (+$200-300/t on 10-15% of electrode cost) hits the P&L only Nov-Jan. RAIN adds the calcined-petroleum-coke anode consumable into aluminium smelters (Carbon EBITDA up INR 1.63B as CPC prices ran $50-100 above the West on China's supply crunch); SMLT the cored-wire leg into steel mills.
themes.driver: Steel/cement output-volume growth driving per-tonne consumables demand; HEG's October price increases landing against needle-coke inflation arriving only Nov-Jan - Q3 is the quarter the margin-maintenance promise is decided.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: RAIN converts byproducts of oil refining (green petroleum coke) and steel production (coal tar) into high-value carbon-based products (CPC, CTP and other carbon products) used as critical raw materials by the aluminium, graphite, carbon black, wood preservation, titanium dioxide and refractory industries. Its Advanced Materials segment further transforms a portion of this carbon output plus petrochemicals into engineered products, chemical intermediates and resins for specialty chemicals, coatings, construction, automotive and petroleum customers, while its Cement segment manufactures and markets OPC and PPC for civil construction and infrastructure within India.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Aluminium industry remains a firm anchor for the Carbon business, supported by infrastructure development, automotive electrification, growing use of lightweight materials and increasing use of advanced carbon-based products in manufacturing
- Several major aluminium smelters committed to capacity expansions and new smelter construction in the US, South Asia and Southeast Asia during 2025, where RAIN is positioned to supply calcined petroleum coke and coal tar pitch
- LME three-month aluminium prices traded above US$3,000 per tonne toward year-end 2025, strengthening demand for carbon-derived products
- Demand conditions evolved gradually through 2025: aluminium and steel producers maintained cautious production schedules in H1 amid uncertain demand, with steel trends uneven across regions depending on infrastructure activity and exports
- Construction sector, the primary growth driver of the Cement segment, remained stable yet moderated, with subdued demand in South India necessitating continued pricing discipline in a competitive environment
- Demand for specialty chemicals and advanced materials was initially measured as customers adopted conservative procurement, but order flows stabilised in H2 2025 leading to gradual recovery across several product categories
- Planned development of the Amaravati capital city project in Andhra Pradesh is expected to provide meaningful support to regional cement demand beginning in 2026
- Long-term structural demand for aluminium and steel continues to be influenced by decarbonisation efforts; near-term production decisions were driven by cost competitiveness and regional capacity utilisation, reflecting cyclical rather than structural adjustment in demand for carbon-based inputs
- Working capital aligned with realistic demand expectations and close monitoring of receivables to support cash conversion and liquidity; net debt remained elevated from earlier-cycle investments but improved EBITDA strengthened leverage metrics
- Long-term outlook for cement remains positive, attributable to continued infrastructure investment and urbanisation across India, despite near-term headwinds from extended monsoon conditions and cyclical softness in regional markets

capital_allocation.body: Repaid 44M USD senior secured notes due April 2025; prioritized working capital buildup due to import quota utilization and higher raw material prices; net debt reduction target of 3.0x EBITDA by 2026; R&D investment in battery anodes as strategic bet

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: During 2025, RAIN received the necessary permissions to initiate a brownfield expansion at its Cement segment's site in Suryapet, India, which will increase clinker capacity from 1.0 to 2.5 million tonnes and expand waste-heat recovery electricity capacity from 5 MW to 12 MW; total cement capacity remained at 4.0 million tonnes across operations in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh pending this expansion. Alongside the Suryapet project, RAIN progressed captive renewable/solar power initiatives at its cement plants (including an onsite solar power capacity expansion of 2.10 MW near a plant) and continued logistics optimisation. For 2026, strategic focus areas at the Cement segment include cost competitiveness through freight optimisation, strengthened quality assurance, upgraded laboratories and additional solar electricity generation, 'supporting the future and a new production line'. RAIN also initiated development of a net-zero roadmap for the Cement segment in collaboration with the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), currently in a baseline-establishment phase covering emissions, water and waste. On the Advanced Materials/Carbon side, RAIN established the Rain Technology Innovation Center in Hamilton, Ontario for carbon-based anode material development and testing, and is running multiple publicly funded R&D projects (OVIN, NGen, CMIF, Canada-Germany ZIM) on graphite purification, coating, upcycling and sustainable supply chains, alongside a North American demonstration facility supporting entry into Battery Anode Material (BAM) markets. Named capex-linked upgrades at the Lake Charles facility include boiler economiser modification/upgrade, boiler feedwater heat exchanger upgrade, baghouse MCC HVAC upgrade and wastewater pretreatment improvements.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Optimistic on CPC and global blending strategy; confident in margin recovery; cautious on Advanced Materials and cement; excited about Canada battery anode R&D; tone is resilient and forward-looking

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Vertically-integrated, global-scale organisation providing a platform to develop higher-margin downstream products
- Scale and process sophistication give flexibility to source raw materials from a wide range of geographies and adjust product mix to meet stringent customer specifications
- Global manufacturing footprint and integrated worldwide logistics network positioned to address raw material supply and product demand on a global basis in both established and emerging markets
- Established supplier to the Chinese battery market with years of experience serving major manufacturers, positioning RAIN in the emerging Battery Anode Material (BAM) space
- Global shared-service centre in India supporting SAP ERP usage across all global facilities, enabling effective internal controls and timely reporting

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Raw material volatility (GPC, coal tar, benzene); European energy cost resurgence; geopolitical trade disruptions; tariff escalation; cement market pricing pressure; delayed recovery in Advanced Materials demand

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Reintroduction of U.S. CPC into India after 6 years is a structural shift enabling global blend arbitrage; HHCR plant's waste-heat steam reuse in Belgium is an underappreciated cost saver; CAQM import liberalization is a regulatory tailwind not priced in by market

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Diversification across Carbon, Advanced Materials and Cement segments to balance risk and mitigate challenges within individual businesses
- Continued emphasis on investment discipline and structural optimisation, including deferring the proposed brownfield expansion of the Cement segment to reassess short-, medium- and long-term regional demand fundamentals before initiating it at a more appropriate time
- In Advanced Materials, gradual increase in participation in higher-value downstream applications (including an initial foray into energy-storage-linked materials) while leveraging core carbon …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CPC price surge and import liberalization in India | Rain Industries Limited | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of lifted import ban and China CPC supply crunch; global blending strategy now operational |
| Rising demand for battery anode materials from EV sector | Rain Industries Limited | beneficiary | Med | Canada demo plant positions RAIN for future BAM supply; not yet revenue-generating but strategic |
| European coal tar scarcity | Other Indian coal tar distillers without global sourcing | loser | Low | RAIN's global logistics advantage creates competitive moat; smaller players may struggle |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Aluminium market] "Supply tightness persists amid Middle East disruptions. Recovery dependent on de-escalation and logistics normalization", and "Elevated LME and energy costs are supporting restarts but may pressure downstream demand."
- [Input prices] The deck flags "Benzene quotations at 12-quarters high" while "Brent Oil & Natural Gas are stabilizing".
- [Trade routes] "Risks remain under active watch, with contingency options supporting continuity"; the Q3 outlook "Remains cautious amid geopolitical, logistics and commodity-market volatility."
- [Cement competition] Cement revenue decline is attributed to "increased competition and decrease in net sales price realisations".
